thread:
Jordan: Heads up — I'm planning a rolling apply for the gpu_pool terraform module tomorrow 02:00 UTC. This is the v1.2.0 -> v1.3.0 bump (param rename + regional fallback). Anyone who needs to block, speak now.
Maria: Quick question — does the new module rename the KMS param? Last week a PR that renamed `kms_key_id` caused a staging plan that wanted to replace the KMS attachment.
Leo: It does introduce `kms_key_ref` and mark `kms_key_id` as deprecated in the docs. If we apply naively, TF will see a change to an input and may want to recreate resources that reference it. I'm recommending a rolling-apply with a state-safe shim.
Maria: Can you show what the risky plan looked like last time?
Leo: Sure — snippet from the staging plan: ```
-/+ aws_kms_key_alias.current (new resource required)
  ~ id: "alias/redwood-prod" => "alias/redwood-prod" # forces replacement due to param rename
  ~ tags: {"env" = "staging"} => {"env" = "staging"}
```
Jordan: That's the exact risk. Our two mitigations: 1) provider-safe alias in module so old inputs map to new ones (no address change), 2) lifecycle `ignore_changes` for `kms_key_id`for a single release while we migrate references. Plan: apply to staging -> us-east1 dev cluster, validate no replacements for KMS, then roll to a single us-west1 GPU pool, monitor for 4 hours, then bulk roll.
Maria: Also noticed the new defaults changed `min_size` from `2` -> `4` if left unset. That would spike committed cost for smaller clusters. Is the release going to change defaults?
Jordan: Good catch — the module author added a regional sizing heuristic. We're going to override via a release var `min_size_override` and keep existing clusters' behaviour. The default in the module will remain the new heuristic but we won't flip prod clusters automatically.
devops-bot: Scheduled job created: `infra/terraform/rollouts/gpu-module/1855551234` -> run window 2028-11-12T02:00:00Z -> approvers: @Jordan, @Maria. Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/run/1855551234
sre-bot: Drift monitor: detected config drift in `us-west1/gpupool-batch-001` at 2028-11-10T18:41:02Z — terraform input `min_size` missing, actual node count 3. No immediate action required, ticket: #INC-5234
Leo: I will add a small migration script to the module repo that does: 1) set `kms_key_ref = kms_key_id` if present, 2) add a `deprecated_kms_key_id` output for one release, 3) include an import snippet: ```bash
# import existing state so param rename doesn't create new resource
terraform state mv module.gpu_pool.aws_kms_key_alias.old module.gpu_pool.aws_kms_key_alias
# or use `terraform import` if alias missing
```
Maria: For rollout procedure — can we do a GitOps staged apply by cluster tag? i.e., apply to `env=staging` then `tag=canary-gpu` (smallest region), then `tag=prod-gpu`? We should keep autoscaler min at 0/1 in canary.
Jordan: Yes, use the `gitops/overlays/gpu-module` branch with three overlays. Our CI will apply overlays in order. I'll update the rollout doc with manual rollback steps (state restore + set `min_size_override=2`).
Leo: I'll open the PR with the shim and migration docs. Also adding a short test: run `terraform plan` in CI with `TF_VAR_kms_key_id` set to existing value to assert no replacement.
Maria: Add a note in the PR about cost impact and tag finance for FYI. We should include a short cost delta: expected committed GPUs +$1.2k/mo if defaults flip.
Jordan: Sounds good. After PR lands, I'll request the scheduled run to proceed. If anyone sees anything blocking, ping me in thread. :thumbsup:
Maria: SGTM. I'll watch staging apply and run the post-apply smoke tests (kv-cache, model loading on one GPU).
Leo: PR is coming — will include the alias, `lifecycle` shim, import snippet, and migration checklist.
sre-bot: Reminder: during rolling apply, set `max_surge = 1` for pools in `high-availability` regions to avoid throttling the autoscaler.
Jordan: Noted. Thanks all.
